ENVR 100.title: Exploring Environmental Science
ENVR 100.description: Introduction to topics in Earth Science, Ecology, Human Health and Energy from an Environmental Science perspective.

ENVR 200.title: Introduction to Environmental Science
ENVR 200.description: Seminars and field trips introducing the major global, regional, and local environmental issues facing human societies.

prerequisite.raw: Open to all students with second-year, or higher, standing

ENVR 200.prerequisiteText: Open to all students with second-year, or higher, standing

ENVR 201.title: Climate Action Lab 1
ENVR 201.description: Community-engaged climate action projects; skill building for climate action. Pass/Fail.

ENVR 205.title: Environmental Science in Practice I
ENVR 205.description: Community building, land connections and academic and career planning in environmental science.

ENVR 240.title: Environmental Problem Solving
ENVR 240.description: Practical and theoretical approaches to tackling complex environmental challenges with emphasis on critical thinking to analyze real-world issues.
ENVR 240.corequisiteText: One of STAT_V 200, 201, BIOL_V 300, STAT_O 205, STAT_O 230

ENVR 300.title: Introduction to Research in Environmental Science
ENVR 300.description: Environmental research. Students investigate research methodologies and reporting in a range of scientific disciplines and fields.

prerequisite.raw: Open to all students with third-year, or higher, standing in the Faculty of Science

ENVR 300.prerequisiteText: Open to all students with third-year, or higher, standing in the Faculty of Science

ENVR 301.title: Climate Action Lab 2
ENVR 301.description: Community-engaged climate action projects; skill building for climate action. Pass/Fail.

ENVR 302.title: Climate Action Lab 1 and 2
ENVR 302.description: Community-engaged climate action projects; skill building for climate action. Pass/Fail

ENVR 305.title: Environmental Science in Practice II
ENVR 305.description: Mentoring, incorporating feedback, strengthening land connections and academic and career planning in environmental science.

ENVR 350.title: Applied Environmental Ethics
ENVR 350.description: The complexities of socio-ecological issues facing practitioners of environmental sciences including ethics and social equity.

ENVR 400.title: Community Project in Environmental Science
ENVR 400.description: Instructor-guided collaboration between student teams and community partners on community-based environmental science projects. Teams articulate project questions and goals, devise methods, conduct research and communicate results.

ENVR 401.title: Climate Action Lab 3
ENVR 401.description: Community-engaged climate action projects; skill building for climate action. Pass/Fail.

ENVR 402.title: Climate Studies and Action Capstone
ENVR 402.description: Instructor-guided collaboration between student teams and community partners on climate action projects.

ENVR 410.title: Energy, Environment, and Society
ENVR 410.description: The role of energy in human societies throughout history and the environmental and social implications of energy use. Coverage of both the science and policy of energy use. Energy supply and demand, energy transitions, analytical tools, impacts, and alternatives.

prerequisite.raw: Fourth-year standing in B.Sc., B.A.Sc. or related programs

ENVR 410.prerequisiteText: Fourth-year standing in B.Sc., B.A.Sc. or related programs

ENVR 420.title: Ecohydrology of Watersheds and Water Systems
ENVR 420.description: Analysis of water resources from a water-in-ecosystem perspective. Application to natural, managed, and urban systems, considering ecological interactions with hydrological processes. Exploration of biogeochemical processes related to water quality, and human impacts on water resources.

prerequisite.raw: Third or fourth-year standing in Science, Applied Science, Land and Food Systems, or Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

ENVR 420.prerequisiteText: Third or fourth-year standing in Science, Applied Science, Land and Food Systems, or Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

ENVR 430.title: Ecological Dimensions of Sustainability
ENVR 430.description: Current issues. Application to agricultural, energy, and resource systems in terrestrial and aquatic contexts. Analysis of complex problems; incorporation of science into novel interdisciplinary solutions.
ENVR 430.prerequisiteText: Class standing 3, and either (1) one of ENVR 300, BIOL 230, FRST 201 or (2) other demonstrated ecology background

ENVR 440.title: Analytical Methods in Sustainability Science
ENVR 440.description: Sustainability analysis through a series of case studies. Example approaches include cost-benefit analysis, trade-offs analysis, and life-cycle analysis. Active learning in a computer lab using real-world data.
ENVR 440.prerequisiteText: One of ENVR 200, ASIC 220, SCIE 220, GEOG 211. Third-year standing

ENVR 448.title: Directed Studies in Environmental Science
ENVR 448.description: Investigation of a topic to be agreed upon by a member of the faculty and the student. Permission of an ENSC advisor and of the supervising faculty member is required prior to registration.

prerequisite.raw: Third year standing in the Faculty of Science

ENVR 448.prerequisiteText: Third year standing in the Faculty of Science

ENVR 449.title: Environmental Science HonoursThesis

children.raw: fourth-year standing in the B.Sc. Environmental Sciences honours program

ENVR 449.prerequisiteText: [ENVR300] and fourth-year standing in the B.Sc. Environmental Sciences honours program

ENVR 450.title: Environmental Policy and Law
ENVR 450.description: The creation, implementation and enforcement of environmental laws and policies at the international, national, and sub-national levels. Examination and critique of laws, principles, and policies dealing with issues such as climate change, pollution, and biological diversity.

ENVR 490.title: Student Directed Seminars in Environmental Sciences
ENVR 490.description: Self-directed, collaborative studies in environmental sciences, in a group-learning environment, initiated and coordinated by senior undergraduate students with the supervision of a faculty advisor. Course structure, enrolment, and delivery methods will comply with the Handbook for Student Directed Seminars.
